decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed increased the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a new target of 3-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Although energy prices have risen further, the expansion remains firm and labor market conditions continue to improve gradually.
changes.explanation: The committee noted that despite higher energy prices, economic expansion is firm and labor conditions are improving.

changes.quote: Pressures on inflation have stayed elevated, but longer-term inflation expectations remain well contained.
changes.explanation: Inflation pressures remain elevated while long-term inflation expectations are still well contained.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors unanimously approved a 25-basis-point increase in the discount rate to 4-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The discount rate was also raised by 25 basis points to 4-1/4 percent.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3-1/4 percent.
Pressures on inflation have stayed elevated, but longer-term inflation expectations remain well contained.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.21% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.94% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.57% would fall by about $9.43 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 5.1%, and employers added an average of 218k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (May 2005); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the committee expects to continue removing policy accommodation at a measured pace. Educational forecast models suggest an 85% chance of a hike at the next meeting.
